faq: Which systems can it read orders from?
Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and many shipping tools such as ShipStation or carrier tracking pages. For custom systems we check what access exists before you order.
How do you stop people seeing someone else's order?
The assistant needs both the order number and the matching email before it shows anything. If they do not match, it shows a generic message and offers a person to contact.
Can the chatbot cancel or change an order?
Only requests, in our Premium package. The assistant records the request and sends it to your team or applies a rule you set. Refunds and edits stay under your control.
What if my store system is old or closed?
Some systems do not allow safe lookups. We tell you before you order. In those cases we can offer a version that explains the process and sends customers to a tracking page.

desc:
A chatbot for order and shipping status questions answers "where is my order" without tying up your staff. Ecom Swift LLC connects an assistant to your store or shipping system so customers can check status safely, using their own order details.

## Why do order status questions take so much support time?

Order status questions take so much time because every customer who has bought something wants to know when it will arrive, and each one asks separately. The answer already exists in your store or carrier system. Staff spend their day looking it up and typing it back.

Without automation, these questions pile up after every sale, shipping delay or holiday rush. Real problems, such as a damaged parcel or a wrong item, get buried in the same inbox. Customers wait longer, and your team spends effort on lookups instead of fixing issues.

## What order-aware chatbots change

An order assistant does the lookup for the customer. They enter an order number and the email used at checkout, the assistant checks the match and shows the current status with a tracking link. No staff time is spent.

This helps in three ways. Customers get an answer at any hour, which reduces anxiety after purchase. Your team receives fewer repeated messages and can focus on exceptions. And messages written for delays or stuck parcels give customers an honest explanation instead of silence, which cuts the angry follow-ups that arrive later.

## What a safe order assistant includes

- A lookup that needs both the order number and the matching email.
- A neutral message when details do not match, which reveals nothing about other orders.
- Clear status wording: received, packed, shipped, delivered, delayed.
- A tracking link for the correct carrier.
- Explanations of your return and exchange rules, written in plain language.
- Prepared messages for delays, lost parcels and customs holds.
- Support for the shipping companies your store really works with.
- Handoff to your team when the status is unclear or the customer is upset.
- Requests to change an address passed to staff, rather than guessed at.
- Cancellations allowed only inside the rules you set.
- A report showing which order questions come up most.

## What we do

First we look at your store or order system and confirm whether it can be read safely. Many platforms provide a standard way to look up orders. If yours does not, or if it is too old or closed to connect without risk, we tell you before you order and suggest another route, such as a simple status page or a form that reaches your team.

When the connection is possible, we build the lookup, add the verification step and write the messages for each status. The Basic package covers lookups and tracking links for one system. The Standard package adds return rules, delay messages, several carriers and handoff. The Premium package adds address change requests, cancellations by your rules, more carriers, reporting and a larger test.

We test with real order cases, including wrong numbers, mismatched emails, split shipments and returned parcels. We do not give the assistant the power to refund or change orders by itself unless you decide that, and even then only inside your written rules.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Ask for two pieces of information before showing any order details.
- Tell customers honestly when a parcel is late.
- Link to the carrier's tracking page.
- Send complex or emotional cases to a person.
- Keep return conditions short and easy to find.

**Avoid:**
- Showing an order after only one weak match, such as a name.
- Letting the bot promise delivery dates the carrier has not confirmed.
- Hiding the contact option when something has gone wrong.
- Allowing cancellations after an order has been packed.
- Storing customer details in the chat longer than needed.

## Who this service is for

It suits an online store whose inbox fills with delivery questions after each campaign. It suits a small business shipping through several carriers that wants one place to see status. It also suits a team that has already set up a chatbot and now wants it to handle the most common request it still sends to staff.

## What we need from you

Tell us which store platform or order system you use and which carriers you ship with. Share your return rules and any delay wording you already use. We ask for collaborator, staff or developer access to the system we connect, with permission to read orders only, unless you request more. We never need passwords.
